title: Council adopts fiscal 2027 budget with no tax rate increase for the third year
summary: The $214 million budget adds two firefighters, a second library bookmobile and $9 million for street repairs, and keeps the tax rate at $0.4875.
body:
The City Council adopted the fiscal 2027 budget on September 22 by a vote of 6 to 1. The $214 million budget takes effect October 1.

What is in it

  • $9 million for street repairs, the most in the city's history.
  • Two new firefighter positions at Station 6.
  • A second bookmobile for neighbourhoods far from a library branch.
  • A 3 percent pay increase for city employees.

The tax rate stays at $0.4875 per $100 of valuation for the third year in a row. The full budget document is on the Finance department page.

title: Cedar Street closed between 4th and 6th for water main repair
summary: Crews are replacing 400 feet of 1960s cast-iron pipe. The street should reopen by Friday, October 9.
body:
Water Utilities crews are replacing 400 feet of water main under Cedar Street between 4th and 6th Streets. The street is closed to through traffic; residents can reach their driveways from 4th Street.

Some homes may have short water outages. Crews will knock on doors at least an hour ahead.

title: Juniper Creek trail extension goes to a public hearing on October 13
summary: Phase 2 would add 3.4 miles of trail from Falls Park to the Eastside library branch.
body: The proposed second phase of the Juniper Creek trail would link Falls Park to the Eastside branch library with 3.4 miles of 12-foot concrete trail, two bridges and lighting. The City Council holds a public hearing on October 13.

title: Fall leaf and limb collection starts November 2
summary: Bag leaves in paper bags and bundle limbs under 4 feet. Collection follows your regular recycling day.
body: Put paper leaf bags and bundled limbs at the curb on your recycling day from November 2 to December 18. Plastic bags will not be collected.

title: National Night Out draws 2,800 residents to 61 block parties
summary: Thank you to every neighbourhood that hosted. Officers and firefighters visited all 61 parties.
body: Residents hosted 61 block parties on October 6 for National Night Out. Police officers, firefighters and council members visited every one.

title: Voter registration deadline for the November 3 election is October 5
summary: The ballot includes a $48 million bond for streets and drainage. Early voting runs October 19 to 30.
body: The November 3 ballot includes Proposition A, a $48 million bond for street and drainage projects. Early voting runs October 19 to 30 at City Hall and the Eastside library branch.

title: New permit portal cuts average review time to eight working days
summary: Since moving permits online in June, the average residential review time has dropped from 15 to 8 working days.
body: Applicants can now upload plans, track reviews and book inspections online. Paper applications are still accepted at City Hall.

title: Library launches free laptop and hotspot lending
summary: Borrow a laptop for two weeks or a hotspot for three with any Juniper Falls library card.
body: The library now lends 60 laptops and 120 hotspots. Ask at any desk.
